**Proof.**

We first establish a change of variables. For any $b > 1$ and any integer $n \geq 1$, set $u = x^n$, so $x = u^{1/n}$ and $dx = \frac{1}{n} u^{1/n - 1}\, du$. The map $\phi(x) = x^n$ is a $C^1$ bijection from $[1, b]$ onto $[1, b^n]$ with $\phi'(x) = nx^{n-1} > 0$. Since $f$ is Riemann integrable on $[1, b^n]$, the substitution theorem for Riemann integrals gives

$$\int_1^b f(x^n)\, dx = \int_1^{b^n} f(u)\,\frac{1}{n}\,u^{1/n - 1}\, du.$$

**Absolute convergence of both sides.** For $u \geq 1$ and $n \geq 1$, the exponent $1/n - 1 \leq 0$, so $u^{1/n - 1} \leq 1$. Hence

$$\int_1^\infty |f(u)|\,\frac{1}{n}\,u^{1/n - 1}\, du \leq \frac{1}{n}\int_1^\infty |f(u)|\, du < \infty,$$

which shows that $\int_1^\infty f(u)\,\frac{1}{n}\,u^{1/n - 1}\, du$ converges absolutely, and likewise $\int_1^\infty f(x^n)\, dx$ converges absolutely. Therefore we may pass to the limit $b \to \infty$ to obtain

$$\int_1^\infty f(x^n)\, dx = \int_1^\infty f(u)\,\frac{1}{n}\,u^{1/n - 1}\, du.$$

**The limit.** Using the bound $u^{1/n - 1} \leq 1$ for $u \geq 1$,

$$\left|\int_1^\infty f(x^n)\, dx\right| = \left|\int_1^\infty f(u)\,\frac{1}{n}\,u^{1/n - 1}\, du\right| \leq \int_1^\infty |f(u)|\,\frac{1}{n}\,u^{1/n - 1}\, du \leq \frac{1}{n}\int_1^\infty |f(u)|\, du.$$

Since $\int_1^\infty |f| < \infty$, the right-hand side tends to $0$ as $n \to \infty$. Therefore

$$\lim_{n \to \infty} \int_1^\infty f(x^n)\, dx = 0. \qquad \blacksquare$$
